newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian govt drops rural health office closures.
newsitem.headline: Australian govt drops rural health office closures.

text.p: The Australian government, which is losing voter support in rural areas, on Friday reversed a decision to close health insurance offices outside of the main cities.

Although Health Minister Michael Wooldridge is solely responsible for the Medicare offices, he announced the decision in a joint statement with the leader of the rural-based National Party, Tim Fischer.

"The strong representations by the government's rural MPs and Senators to retain the existing Medicare offices in rural communities were compelling and well argued," the ministers said in a joint statement.
"Cabinet accepted that the inconvenience for people in rural communities would be much greater than in metropolitan areas because of the larger distances between country towns," they said.

Polls show voters fleeing the conservative Liberal-National government for the new One Nation party of populist independent MP Pauline Hanson, who stands for a return to tariff protection and an end to Aboriginal welfare and Asian immigration.
Hanson's support is strongest in rural areas.
